title: Stephen A. Smith Is 'Starting to Feel Really, Really Sorry' for Cowboys Owner Jerry Jones - NewsBreak
text:
By Angelo Guinhawa ,
6 hours ago Stephen A. Smith is beginning to feel sympathy for Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones after another disappointing finish exposed several issues surrounding the team. The Cowboys suffered a 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in a game that raised more questions about the decisions Jones made during the offseason.
Dallas had opportunities to control the outcome late in the game but ultimately watched Baltimore secure the victory on a last-second field goal. The result added another frustrating chapter to a season in which the Cowboys have struggled to consistently turn their talent into winning football.
Dec 24, 2023; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones signs a helmet prior to the game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jasen Vinlove-USA TODAY Sports Smith pointed toward the coaching decisions surrounding the team as part of the problem. Brian Schottenheimer is leading the offense after being chosen to take over as head coach, and the Cowboys have placed significant responsibility on him to guide the team through critical situations late in games.
The defensive side of the football has also become a concern, particularly after the Cowboys allowed Baltimore to put together enough offense to remain in contention throughout the contest. Dallas entrusted its defense to a first-time defensive coordinator who entered the season with a strong reputation despite being only 34 years old.
Stephen A. Smith Feels Sorry for Dallas Cowboys Owner Jerry Jones Nov 24, 2023; Austin, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones on the field at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium before the game between the Texas Longhorns and the Texas Tech Red Raiders. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-USA TODAY Sports Smith shared his thoughts about Jones, particularly after his team was defeated by the Ravens in Brazil. This can be seen in a video posted by ESPN.
“As it pertains to Jerry Jones, I’m starting to feel really, really sorry for what I’m seeing because again, sometimes het gets in his own way a lot of times he’s gotten in his own way,” Smith said. “We all know that. And one can easily make the argument that he’s done it again”
For Jones, those decisions ultimately fall back on the choices he made while shaping the organization. Smith’s argument centers on the idea that the Cowboys owner has repeatedly placed himself in difficult situations through personnel and coaching decisions, leaving him to watch the consequences unfold when the team struggles.
The loss to Baltimore provided another example of how quickly a promising opportunity can disappear for Dallas. With Schottenheimer running the team and a relatively inexperienced defensive coordinator overseeing the defense, the Cowboys now face continued pressure to prove that the structure Jones selected can produce better results when the stakes become highest.
